description: A random voltage generator with a drawn probability curve: nine knobs weight how often the output lands at nine points spread across -5V to +5V.

params.text: The probability weight at -5V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at -3.75V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at -2.5V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at -1.25V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at 0V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at +1.25V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at +2.5V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at +3.75V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter.
The probability weight at +5V, 0 to 10; the nine weights are read against each other, so only their relative sizes matter. Constant distribution on the menu leaves this knob unused.
Sets the rate of the internal clock in octaves around C4's 261.63Hz, -10 at the left through to +10 at the right.
Sets how long the output takes to travel from the old value to the new one, an instant jump at the left through to 1 second at the right.
LIN travels between values at a steady rate; EXP follows a curve that starts slowly and finishes fast.

inputs.text: Adds its voltage to that knob's weight, and the total is held between 0 and 10.
While this is patched the internal clock is switched off and a new value is drawn on each rising edge here.
Adds twice its voltage to RATE, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Adds a tenth of its voltage to SMOOTH, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.

outputs.text: The generated voltage, -5V to +5V, travelling towards each new value at the rate SMOOTH sets.

notes: A newly placed module has RATE at its far right, which draws a new value several times per sample, so the output is noise until RATE is turned down or a clock is patched to TRIG.
With SMOOTH at 0 the output steps straight to each new value, which makes the module a sample and hold on its own random source.
The drawing between the knob rows is the current probability curve across the output range; it shows the weights and cannot be clicked or dragged.
menu: Constant distribution (instead of linear) — gives every voltage inside one of the eight intervals the same chance, instead of sloping from one knob's weight to the next.
